style.visual_cues: Combine dots, zigzags, stripes, circles, and irregular geometry with bold contrasting colors. Keep the headline readable and use patterns to establish rhythm. Alternate shapes, elastic offsets, and pattern handoffs while limiting simultaneous movement and avoiding rapid full-frame flashing.
style.note: A supplemental design reference; not claimed as a directly named style in the source collection.

recommended_stack.name: HyperFrames
recommended_stack.runtime: HTML composition in browser; CLI orchestration in Node.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Primary pipeline for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Visual construction and motion design remain owned by the selected style renderer and motion engine.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP
suggested_libraries.purpose: Build a paused, seekable timeline and register it with HyperFrames after construction is complete.

recommended_stack.style_application: Compose the output of the selected visual and motion layers. Supply seekable time or integrate baked assets; do not replace the style-specific rendering or motion method with framework defaults.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: Use HyperFrames by default. Fall back to Remotion only when the documented fallback condition is met, and record the reason. Do not mix framework APIs.

recommended_stack.name: SVG
recommended_stack.purpose: Draw scalable shapes, icons, strokes, clipping paths, and masks.
recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Memphis Design according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.name: GSAP
recommended_stack.purpose: Coordinate tweens, staggered actions, and a paused, seekable timeline driven by deterministic video time.
recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Memphis Design according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.name: @remotion/shapes
recommended_stack.purpose: Generate standard SVG geometric shapes such as circles, rectangles, and stars.

recommended_stack.name: Remotion
recommended_stack.runtime: React in browser; rendering orchestrated by Node.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Conditional fallback pipeline for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Visual construction and motion design remain owned by the selected style renderer and motion engine.
recommended_stack.style_application: Compose the output of the selected visual and motion layers. Supply seekable time or integrate baked assets; do not replace the style-specific rendering or motion method with framework defaults.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

recommended_stack.name: Motion
recommended_stack.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
recommended_stack.purpose: Optional animation of DOM or SVG layers for Memphis Design. Preserve the style-specific timing and visual cues; verify deterministic video seeking before use.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Motion is an optional layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP timeline contract. Explicitly synchronize and verify seeking; use GSAP when that integration is not established. Use motion/react only within a React component runtime.

recommended_stack.name: chroma.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally validate colors, derive controlled palette variants, interpolate colors, and check foreground/background contrast.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Start with task-provided colors and the style visual_cues. Keep a shared, deterministic palette and named color tokens. Generate gradients or interpolate colors only when the style permits them; keep limited-palette, monochrome, pixel, and print treatments discrete where required. Evaluate animated color from shared composition time. Check contrast against the actual composited background; a two-color ratio alone does not verify text over transparency, gradients, textures, or video. Pass output through the selected renderer's color API and preserve its color-space handling. Native CSS/SVG colors remain sufficient when no color processing is needed.
recommended_stack.style_application: Read palette.tokens, palette.constraints and palette.agent_instruction for Memphis Design. Validate approved colors and assess readable existing token pairs with chroma-js. Use palette.gradient only when enabled and appropriate. Preserve task/reference colors exactly; optional suggested tokens are fallback inputs, not permission to recolor assets.

recommended_stack.name: mo.js
recommended_stack.runtime: browser DOM and SVG; initialize after target elements are mounted
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally generate and animate geometric shapes, radial bursts, swirl accents and existing HTML elements for expressive 2D motion graphics.
recommended_stack.import_guidance: Import mojs from '@mojs/core' using a compatible bundler or the documented browser build. Verify exports and signatures against the installed version. Keep DOM-dependent construction out of server-side rendering.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Use mo.js as an optional effects layer, not a video renderer or replacement for the HyperFrames timeline registration contract. Build effects once, pause independent playback, and evaluate normalized setProgress values from shared seekable composition time. Account explicitly for local start, delay, duration, repeats, yoyo and end visibility using the installed API. Preserve the registered GSAP timeline as the HyperFrames clock and synchronize mo.js through the selected framework update mechanism; verify updates on direct seeks rather than relying only on playback callbacks. For Remotion, use its mounted browser lifecycle and frame-derived time. Assign each animated property one owner; use nested wrappers if GSAP controls scene placement while mo.js controls an inner effect.
recommended_stack.determinism_guidance: Resolve random particle properties into explicit reproducible values before building the effect. Do not regenerate random values with generate() during export or depend on live click triggers. Keep effect state derivable from requested time. Verify initial visibility, direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks against sequential playback, including delays and end holds. If the chosen mo.js effect cannot be reliably evaluated this way, recreate it with the existing GSAP/SVG route rather than introducing a separate playback clock.
recommended_stack.color_guidance: Use the resolved palette tokens directly for stroke and fill. Keep limited and monochrome palettes discrete. Animate color interpolation only when the style and palette permit it; do not adopt example-code colors or add arbitrary particle hues. Preserve typography, approved assets and material treatment.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: Choose mo.js when its shape, burst or swirl modules simplify a meaningful effect. Existing GSAP or native SVG can remain sufficient. Supported shape-property animation does not establish arbitrary path morphing, fluid physics, handwriting, character rigging, frame-by-frame drawing or automatic music analysis.
recommended_stack.style_application: Optional geometric bursts, shape sequences and playful accents that follow the Memphis pattern system. Limit simultaneous effects and preserve headline legibility.

recommended_stack.name: Matter.js
recommended_stack.runtime: browser or Node.js for simulation baking
recommended_stack.purpose: Simulate 2D rigid bodies with gravity, collisions, restitution, friction and constraints; render their poses with the chosen visual layer.
recommended_stack.style_application: Give selected Memphis circles and blocks collision-aware bounces or stacks while keeping most patterns anchored and the headline readable.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: For video, precompute poses with seeded initial conditions and fixed Engine.update steps, then sample cached states by composition time for direct and backward seeking. Do not drive exports with Runner.run or a wall-clock loop. For interactive pages, a live runner is appropriate. This is 2D rigid-body physics, not 3D, fluid or true soft-body simulation; authored deformation remains a separate layer. Bodies.fromVertices may need poly-decomp for concave shapes. Keep critical text and imagery readable.

tech.implementation: Build SVG patterns and reusable shape groups. Stagger selected movements and elastic accents instead of animating every pattern at once.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Memphis Design without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

style.executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Memphis Design video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. Check the primary framework first; use tech.framework_selection.fallback only when the documented fallback_condition is met, and record the verified reason. An existing React project alone is not sufficient reason to switch.
1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Combine dots, zigzags, stripes, circles, and irregular geometry with bold contrasting colors. Keep the headline readable and use patterns to establish rhythm. Alternate shapes, elastic offsets, and pattern handoffs while limiting simultaneous movement and avoiding rapid full-frame flashing. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Build SVG patterns and reusable shape groups. Stagger selected movements and elastic accents instead of animating every pattern at once. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional mo.js effects: consult the @mojs/core entry in tech.recommended_stack when shape, burst, swirl or HTML effects support the scene. Follow its style_application, integration_guidance, determinism_guidance and color_guidance. Preserve the resolved palette and reading holds. Build effects once, pause independent playback, and drive progress from shared composition time; verify direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks. Keep one owner per animated property and preserve the selected video framework lifecycle. Do not use live click triggers or regeneration during video export. Use the existing GSAP/SVG route if an effect cannot satisfy deterministic seeking.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

source_frame_review.sampling_limitation: One frame at each available second 01–08. No continuous motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes verified. Color families are visual observations; whole-frame measured dominant colors are not semantic background tokens.
source_frame_review.guidance: Choose scene-dependent backgrounds and readable coordinated colors. Separate material colors, source demonstration choices and surrounding UI/letterboxing. Existing swatches are examples, not permanent canvas restrictions. Keep explicit user-approved colors and medium-defining constraints. Only sampled seconds, not continuous motion or audio, were visually reviewed.

sources.style_evidence: Seconds 4–6: scattered zigzags, squiggles, outline rings, triangles, x-crosses and dots in bold contrasting colors as a rhythmic confetti layer.
sources.palette_lesson: The background changes on purpose with each life stage, and that is the main lesson. The opening is near-black navy for an abstract, pre-life pulse. Childhood uses naturalistic sky-teal, pale green and green with a warm yellow sun. Adolescence uses a saturated indigo-to-magenta gradient with a striped warm sun and neon cyan, yellow and orange confetti. Adulthood uses desaturated stepped greys with only small red and brown accents. These specific hues are this author's choices for this story, not rules of the style. What defines the style: each scene has a coherent flat palette of about 3–6 families; a thin white line/HUD layer stays readable on every background; a small warm accent (red heart, red tie, red ball) carries over between scenes; and saturation and value shifts are used as storytelling, not decoration. For new subjects, choose the field from the emotion of each chapter. Options include deep teal night ocean, dusty terracotta desert at dusk, cold blue-white winter morning, lime-and-mint spring, warm amber interior lamplight, slate-blue rain, and black-and-violet club space. Then check that the white line and HUD keep enough contrast; on very light fields, switch the line to dark ink.

sources.style_evidence: The backgrounds rotate through bold flat fields with stripes, dot grids and concentric rings, using contrasting candy colors (yellow/pink/cyan, mint, violet, indigo). Pattern handoffs happen at each cut.
sources.palette_lesson: These colors are the creator's choices for this short, not a fixed recipe. Each scene uses one saturated, nearly flat background family (golden-yellow stripes, deep indigo, slate blue with a screenshot collage, mint, periwinkle, a yellow/pink/cyan wipe) and changes family at every hard cut to mark a new idea. The parts that stay constant are what define the style: a pastel mascot with a black contour, caption type in white or yellow fill with a near-black stroke, a white outer keyline and a hard offset shadow, plus small multicolor confetti. The heavy dark stroke plus white halo is what keeps captions legible on any field, light or dark. For new subjects, choose the background from the topic and mood. Options include: deep teal or ink navy for tech or night topics, coral or tomato red for urgency, a soft lilac or sky-blue dot grid for calm explainers, charcoal with a neon-lime ring pulse for gaming, warm terracotta or olive for food or lifestyle, or a desaturated photo or screenshot wall as evidence. Keep one dominant field per scene with a quieter same-hue pattern (dots, stripes or rings at low contrast), and reserve the most saturated accent (yellow or hot pink here) for the key word. Recheck contrast between the mascot's pastel fill and the field: pale lilac on mint or butter yellow relies entirely on the black contour.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of Memphis Design, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

suggested_combinations.selection_guidance: Memphis alone works for playful brand and pattern pieces. Choose a hybrid for short social content needing emphasis captions or when accents need a disciplined motion principle.

suggestions.video_application: Captions pop in on stressed words with navy outlines on pink, teal or yellow, framed by zigzags; patterns hand off between cuts.

productionPolicy.principle: Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique.
productionPolicy.style_renderer: Owns visual construction: drawing, geometry, materials, lighting, typography, masks, textures, and specialist asset generation. Use the style-specific recommended technologies and implementation guidance.
productionPolicy.motion_engine: Owns trajectories, transforms, easing, transitions, deformation, and simulation. Select engines or algorithms appropriate to the action, with one owner for each animated property.
productionPolicy.render_pipeline: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.
productionPolicy.integration: Visual and motion layers expose deterministic state at composition time, or supply baked assets or frame sequences. The pipeline supplies seekable time and composes their output. Timeline registration and frame hooks are integration adapters, not substitutes for style-specific rendering or motion.
productionPolicy.selection: Choose only needed stack entries. A technology may serve multiple roles, but document its actual responsibility. Optional authoring, interaction, color, and preprocessing tools are not mandatory renderers or motion engines.

motionReferences.name: Scroll-Driven Pinned Hero Recomposition
motionReferences.description: The hero stage remains pinned while its internal composition transforms continuously. In the public example, hands separate from their meeting point, a ring enlarges, the central headline clears, and text fragments arrive in the corners. The stable anchor is the stage; the hero's internal objects may move.
motion_sequence: Establish a pinned hero stage with a central subject arrangement and headline.
Separate selected internal elements, enlarge a focal ring or equivalent form, and clear the centered headline.
Bring supporting text into corner or peripheral positions to complete a new arrangement without a cut, then hold and release the pinned stage when the page continues.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Keep the stage fixed in the video canvas while keyframing its internal elements through the recomposition. The main objects may separate, scale, or relocate; do not freeze them merely because the stage is pinned. Preserve framework clip timing and readable text windows.

Preload fonts and preserve reading holds during headline-to-peripheral-copy handoff.

motionReferences.executable_prompt_template:
Consider {{motion_pattern}} for {{subject}} in {{visual_style}}, using {{render_pipeline}}. Define a fixed hero stage and an initial-to-final internal layout through {{motion_parameters}}. Coordinate separation of selected elements, expansion of a focal form, departure of the central headline, and arrival of supporting copy in peripheral positions without a cut. Adapt the example objects to the topic. For video, keyframe the internal recomposition on a fixed canvas; for interactive output, pin the outer stage and animate inner wrappers. Preserve the style grid and reading order, and do not confuse the pinned stage with a frozen subject. Resolve library choices from this pattern's tech guidance and the catalog library_options, and follow render_contract. This is adaptable design guidance rather than an official library preset. Verify direct, backward, and sequential seeks; Canvas or WebGL layers must repaint explicitly on seek.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.

interaction.progress_driver: For an interactive page, pin a defined hero region over a finite scroll range and map progress to staged recomposition.
interaction.exit_behavior: Release the pin without a layout jump; preserve continuity into the next section.

motionReferences.audio_direction_prompt: Based on the topic, mood, medium, and existing audio requirements, suggest whether this action benefits from a restrained sound accent, ambience, music synchronization, or silence. Do not attach a mandatory sound to the pattern or compete with narration.
verification: Seek directly to the start, intermediate states, and end, then compare them with sequential playback.
Check legibility, composition, material consistency, clipping, and visual continuity.
For interactive delivery, check the applicable hover, scroll, keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion behavior; video export must remain independent of live input.
Check that the anchor remains stable while supporting elements retain readable alignment.
For interactive output, inspect pin entry and release for jumps; for video, confirm no scroll dependency.
Check the stated action order and secondary-detail choices against the intended recipe; do not substitute a different motion merely because it shares the title.
motionReferences.adaptation_guidance: The hands, ring, number of text fragments, and exact corner positions are example content. Topic-specific assets may substitute while preserving a fixed stage and continuous transformation of its internal composition. Pinning does not mean every internal subject must remain stationary.

motionReferences.name: Scroll-Driven Chaptered Scene Transition
motionReferences.description: Scroll progress coordinates a handoff between narrative chapters. An outgoing scene yields to an incoming scene through a chosen fade, wipe, panel rotation, or shared-element move; text and media states change with the same progress. Clear start and end states preserve reading order in both scroll directions.
motion_sequence: Establish the outgoing chapter and a readable closing state.
Across a defined progress window, coordinate outgoing and incoming scene states with one selected transition treatment and synchronized copy.
Resolve the incoming chapter into its readable state before beginning the next handoff; reversing progress retraces the same transition.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Schedule chapter windows and transition intervals on composition time. Explicitly choose the handoff type. If the style requires a continuous shot, use a coherent camera or spatial handoff instead of an incompatible cut.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP
suggested_libraries.purpose: Create a paused, seekable timeline for progress, transforms, masks, and controlled easing.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP ScrollTrigger
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional interactive-web adapter: bind normalized progress to scroll. Do not require live scrolling for video export.

suggested_libraries.name: PixiJS
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional 2D implementation of Scroll-Driven Chaptered Scene Transition using sprites, graphics, masks, or layered containers. Preserve the selected style; use Three.js when true 3D geometry is required.
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use a private ticker and disable autoplay with autoStart: false and sharedTicker: false; stop any already-started application. Load assets, derive scene state directly from composition time, and call app.render() explicitly on updates and seeks. Calling ticker.update() alone does not make cumulative simulation seekable.

suggested_libraries.name: Motion
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional DOM or SVG implementation of Scroll-Driven Chaptered Scene Transition using controlled keyframes or sequences. Verify synchronization with the selected video framework before adopting this route.
suggested_libraries.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Pause playback and set animation.time in seconds from composition time, then verify that forward, backward, and direct seeks update the visible result. Motion is an optional animation layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP registration contract; keep the registered GSAP timeline as the framework clock and explicitly synchronize Motion. Use motion/react only within mounted React components.

suggested_libraries.name: tldraw
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optionally author diagram, annotation, or card assets for Scroll-Driven Chaptered Scene Transition. Export layers or structured scene data; animate them using the video timeline.
suggested_libraries.runtime: mounted React editor in browser; exported assets for video composition
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Author diagrams and artwork in a mounted React editor, then export SVG or raster assets using editor.getSvgString or editor.toImage. Await export and split layers deliberately when separate animation is required; a flattened image does not preserve editable shapes. Animate those assets in the chosen framework. Verify signatures against the installed SDK; tldraw is not a video renderer or an automatic timeline adapter.

tech.implementation: Use defined outgoing and incoming scene layers with bounded opacity, mask, or transform states. Tie the full handoff to normalized progress, including copy visibility, rather than firing unrelated enter/exit animations. Interactive output can scrub a GSAP timeline over a finite scroll interval; video uses composition time. Keep framework-owned clip visibility separate from inner transition layers and evaluate reverse or direct seeks without stale scene state.
tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motionReferences.name: Radial Logo Burst
motionReferences.description: Stage a central mark, repeated outward white circular waves at a deliberate pulse tempo, coordinated rays and a compact party-popper burst of white and dark squares, triangles, circles and crosses. Keep tumbling confetti close around the icon; a strong sudden forward impulse toward the viewer slows into a very brief airborne hang, then a natural gravity-driven fall, never a canvas-wide distribution. Use an expanding circular mask for palette inversion while retaining the mark center. Let the burst decay into a stable logo hold; keep later particles subordinate. Use the icon center as the popper exit: pieces begin tiny at that point, shoot forward toward the viewer with a small spread around the center, never an upward launch, increase in apparent size, overlap in front of the icon, briefly hang and then fall. Keep the burst compact; express depth with coherent perspective scale and layer ordering.
motion_sequence: Establish one centered approved mark and its initial field.

Release successive soft circular waves from the fixed mark center at regular beat intervals. Emit a compact cluster of varied white and dark confetti shapes around the icon: a powerful quick forward launch toward the viewer, rotation and tumbling, a very short airborne hang, then a natural accelerating downward fall. Keep confetti local to the icon even as waves expand beyond it. Use the icon center as the popper exit: pieces begin tiny at that point, shoot forward toward the viewer with a small spread around the center, never an upward launch, increase in apparent size, overlap in front of the icon, briefly hang and then fall. Keep the burst compact; express depth with coherent perspective scale and layer ordering.
Expand a circular mask to invert the field and mark palette, then let accents decay into a stable identity hold.

motionReferences.name: Word Smash Cuts
motionReferences.description: Replace short words or phrases through clean, rapid cuts, changing the full-screen background and foreground contrast on each phrase. Build anticipation with a brief punctuation sequence, then increase typographic scale for emphasis. Keep readable holds and avoid automatic glitch or spring effects.
motion_sequence: Hold a short lead-in; optional punctuation steps build anticipation without moving the layout.
Cut directly between word cards with coordinated background and foreground color changes. Use varying but readable phrase holds.
Let an emphasis phrase fill or deliberately cross the frame edges, then hold a clear final message.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Schedule hard word-card cuts and coordinated color changes on the composition timeline. Keep the typography crisp and the palette approved. Match actual music beats only when audio timing has been inspected; this source review assessed visual frames only.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP
suggested_libraries.purpose: Create a paused, seekable timeline for progress, transforms, masks, and controlled easing.

tech.implementation: Preserve a readable starting phrase, then release outgoing glyphs with bounded rotation/downward displacement. Reveal the incoming phrase in deliberate word-sized steps; differentiate the emphasis word and hold the conclusion. Choose pauses from meaning; use verified audio timing only when available. Use the selected style renderer and one seekable timeline. Inspect glyph assets or approved mark geometry first. Preview is a schematic Canvas study, not the source video or a prescribed production renderer.
tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Preserve the chosen visual medium and inspect actual geometry/assets before selecting a renderer.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use one owner per animated property and a paused seekable composition timeline.

adapt_or_omit_when: Use when concise copy can carry the story and the selected style permits abrupt color-field changes.
Omit for dense explanatory text or gentle illustrative sequences.
Use approved palette colors; the reference lime and magenta are examples, not mandatory colors.

motionReferences.executable_prompt_template: Build Word Smash Cuts for {{subject}} in {{visual_style}}. Use concise word/phrase cards with crisp typography, direct cuts and coordinated contrasting background changes. Start with an optional short anticipation/punctuation beat, then use quick readable holds and an oversized emphasis phrase. Preserve the selected palette and reading order; do not add glitches, bouncing or slides unless requested. Schedule deterministic states from composition time and verify seeks before/at/after every cut. Use actual audio beat timing only if inspected. Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export.

interaction.progress_driver: Drive each state from deterministic composition time. Adapt pointer or other interaction only when the delivery requires it.
interaction.exit_behavior: Settle into a readable final state; reduced motion shows the completed composition.

motionReferences.audio_direction_prompt: Based on the topic, mood, medium, and existing audio requirements, suggest whether this action benefits from a restrained sound accent, ambience, music synchronization, or silence. Do not attach a mandatory sound to the pattern or compete with narration.
verification: Verify copy and background change at exactly the same scheduled cut.
Verify phrases hold long enough to read and meaningful emphasis drives scale changes.
Check deterministic direct/backward seeks and stable final frame.
motionReferences.adaptation_guidance: Screened against all 135 styles. Use style-specific motion reference guidance; preserve each medium/palette and select only if the scene has appropriate concise copy.

source_evidence.sampling: 72 artwork-only frames at 12 fps. Presenter area excluded; no audio beat synchronization verified.
source_evidence.observed: Lead-in on lime with incremental ellipsis; cream headline on near-black, black word on lime, cream word on magenta, oversized green wording against near-black. Sharp changes with reading holds.
